newsitem.title: USA: New York State unemployment rate holds at 6.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: New York State unemployment rate holds at 6.2 pct.

text.p: New York State's unemployment rate held at 6.2 percent for the third month in a row.
"Employment advanced in every industry division in June except governments," said Thomas A. Rodick, director of the Division of Research and Statistics.
New York's unemployment rate, after seasonal adjustment, was 6.3 percent in June, unchanged since January 1997.
The metropolitan areas seem to have increased in jobs from 0.1 percent to 0.9 percent while the unemployment rates either stayed the same or fell.
In New York City the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose 10 percent in June up from 9.6 percent in May.
Unemployment rose because the number of City residents who were looking for work grew by 11,000.

The June unemployment numbers show that there continues to be two New York City economies. One is tied to Wall Street and tourisim and is booming. The other is associated with those job seekers without high-tech skills and whio are being left behind in job growth.
"This shows the need for an agressive policy to create entry-level jobs for City residents." said Alan G. Hevesi, New York City Comptroller.
